title: Overview of Health Status among Roma Population in Romania: A Scoping Review
content: Background: Roma are widely recognized as Europe ‘s largest ethnic minority and in-dependent estimates suggest that up to two million people live in Romania. Despite well-documented socioeconomic disadvantage, no prior review has synthesized evi-dence on the health status of Roma in Romania. Objectives: This scoping review mapped the literature on healthcare access, quality of life, chronic disease burden and communicable disease exposure among Roma communities in Romania. Methods: Us-ing the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we con-ducted a systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Science Direct and supplemented by grey literature and reference-list screening, for studies published 2010–2025 in English or Romanian. Results: Thirty-nine sources (35 studies and 4 in-stitutional reports) met the inclusion criteria. Roma communities experience a life-expectancy gap of 3.5–4.6 years, markedly lower preventive-care uptake (39% vs 71% in the general population), and high rates of being uninsured (42–59%). Chronic disease burden was substantially higher than in the general population: hypertension prevalence ranged 33–67%, type 2 diabetes from 10–29%, and obesity from 32–62%, with evidence of earlier onset and more severe complications, including higher pro-gression to chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. Health-related quality of life and mental health indicators were uniformly worse among Roma. Evidence on communicable diseases was sparse but suggested elevated hepatitis B/C prevalence and greater severity of measles and COVID-19. Conclusions: Roma communities in Romania experience markedly poorer health outcomes across nearly all domains ex-amined, driven by intersecting socioeconomic, structural and behavioral determinants.
